theme: relative strength against the broad universe
trace:
The strategy aims to exploit the phenomenon where stocks with higher relative strength outperform the broader market over time. This is based on the behavioral finance theory that optimistic investors may drive up prices of outperforming stocks, creating a positive feedback loop. Relative strength can persist due to惯性（惯性） and self-reinforcing market sentiment.

The rule would involve selecting a portfolio consisting of top N (e.g., 10) stocks with the highest relative strength ratios against the broader universe index (such as the S&P BSE Sensex or NIFTY). These stocks are re-evaluated weekly to adjust the portfolio, ensuring it consistently holds the strongest performers. This approach leverages the tendency of markets to favor winners and could potentially generate alpha by capitalizing on sustained outperformance.

The signal for this equity strategy is based on the Relative Strength Index (RSI). For each stock in the market universe, calculate the RSI using daily open, high, low, close prices. The RSI lookback period can be set to 14 days, a common choice in technical analysis. On any given day, rank all stocks by their RSI values, where higher RSI indicates stronger relative performance. Select the top N (e.g., 10) stocks with the highest RSI ratios against the broader market index (such as S&P BSE Sensex or NIFTY). This ranking and selection process are performed weekly to update the portfolio with the current strongest performers, aiming to capitalize on sustained outperformance driven by positive market sentiment.

This strategy involves holding a top-N portfolio of stocks (e.g., N=10) selected based on their relative strength as indicated by the RSI. Each selected stock would be given an equal weight within the portfolio, ensuring no single stock dominates the position sizing. To manage risk, the total loss limit for the portfolio can be set to a predefined percentage, say 5%, of the total capital invested. This limits potential drawdowns and helps in maintaining a balanced exposure to market volatility. Regular re-evaluation ensures the portfolio remains aligned with the strongest performers, potentially enhancing alpha generation while controlling downside risk.
